previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism, and long-standing anemia was admitted for malaise and worsening abdominal pain. She was found to have severe anemia with a hemoglobin of 4.3 g/dL and received three units of packed red blood cells. A CT scan showed no active gastrointestinal bleeding but confirmed diverticulosis. Her anemia was attributed to vitamin B12 deficiency and possible myelodysplastic syndrome, leading to initiation of B12 injections. Congestive heart failure symptoms worsened post-transfusion but improved with IV furosemide. Warfarin was resumed given no evidence of bleeding. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient hematology follow-up, continued B12 replacement, and management of chronic conditions.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Diverticulosis of large intestine without perforation or abscess without bleeding
Presence of left artificial hip joint

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:   ___ with CHF, crackles L lung base. 2 days abd pain, greatest
LLQ.  // CXR: Eval for pleural effusion or acute process. CT Abd/Pelvis: Eval
for ischemic colitis

TECHNIQUE:  AP and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: 

There are bibasilar opacities superimposed on chronic increased interstitial
markings more superiorly.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is grossly unchanged. 
No acute osseous abnormalities, degenerative changes seen at the AC and
glenohumeral joints bilaterally.

IMPRESSION: 

Chronic interstitial process, potentially due to edema or other interstitial
process.  More dense bibasilar opacities could be atelectasis although
superimposed infection would be possible, particularly on the right.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS

INDICATION:  ___ with CHF, crackles L lung base. 2 days abd pain, greatest
LLQ.NO_PO contrast  // CXR: Eval for pleural effusion or acute process. CT
Abd/Pelvis: Eval for ischemic colitis

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 747 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made with CTA abdomen and pelvis from ___ and CTA chest and CT abdomen pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST:  The previously seen chronic interstitial changes and
ground-glass opacities are again noted on the lung bases.  New areas of
possible consolidative opacity are noted in the right lung base. There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
A small hypodensity likely representing a renal cyst is noted the upper pole
of the left kidney.  There is no perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops demonstrate
normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  Diverticulosis is
seen throughout the colon, without evidence of acute diverticulitis.  The
colon and rectum are otherwise unremarkable.  There is no evidence of ischemic
colitis.  The appendix is normal.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The reproductive organs are unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Mild/moderate
atherosclerotic disease is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
Degenerative changes are seen throughout the visualized spine, most prominent
at L5-S1.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No acute intra-abdominal process, no evidence of ischemic colitis.

2. Diverticulosis without evidence of acute diverticulitis.

3.  New areas of possible consolidative opacity noted in the right lung base
superimposed on a background of a chronic interstitial abnormality.  This
could be due to atelectasis although superimposed infection could be
considered in the correct clinical setting.
